summary_paraphrase: A pup on a farm cannot fall asleep, slips out into the moonlit night and meets five night animals in turn, each of which agrees to be his friend; tired out by play he goes home, his mother explains that these friends are nocturnal and that he needs sleep, and he sleeps through the night under the smiling moon.

beats.function: everyone asleep but the pup; he cannot sleep
he goes out and finds the night beautiful
one night animal per page, same friendship exchange each time
play tires him; he goes home
mother names nocturnal animals and hugs him
sleeps through the night under the moon

characters.name: Tinku

characters.change: from restless and alone to tired, befriended and asleep

characters.name: Ma
characters.change: asleep at the start, explains and comforts at the end

characters.name: owl

characters.name: the moon
characters.relation_to_protagonist: silent smiling watcher, opens and closes the book

repetition.description: the same question and answer about friendship closes each meeting
repetition.why: five returns let a listener answer before the page does; the line never changes, which suits winding down

repetition.description: one new night animal per page, introduced by a sight or sound and a self-introduction
repetition.why: predictable pattern with a new animal each time

repetition.description: the smiling moon on the first and last page
repetition.why: frames the night with the same calm watcher

notes: The moon's face is a silent companion on the first, third and last page.
The owl page is the most startling image; the text keeps it friendly.
Every page has text: the story works read aloud without pictures.

strengths: a home-away-home bedtime frame: the last page returns to the mother and the same moon at the lowest intensity
a friendship refrain repeated five times that a listener can join
the night is reframed from lonely to friendly without any danger
weaknesses: the middle is a list; the five meetings have no rising stakes
the mother's last speech explains a fact (nocturnal animals) and a rule (you must sleep) in words

anti_patterns.note: the mother states why he must sleep

child_appeal_heuristic.rationale: Scores are the analyst's reading of the pages, not observations of children.
child_appeal_heuristic.label: Research heuristic — not validated

age_suitability.notes: No peril. Highest research intensity 3/5 (about 2 on the engine's 0-3 scale) on pages 4-8, settling to 0 on the last page. The pup leaving home alone at night is fantasy; a MagicPaper version would keep the child near home or with a companion.

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address

repetition.end_rhyme_note: heuristic: consecutive lines sharing a final two letters
